report.source_text: Emergency whole-spine contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a huge intramedullary thoracic lesion extending from T5 to T8 that was hyperintense in T2-weighted images (Figure 1a), with scattered enhancement after the injection of contrast (Figure 1b). Additionally, there was a round intradural extramedullary mass lesion at the L1 and L2 levels causing a compression effect on the conus medullaris that was isointense in T2-wighted images (Figure 1c), with homogenous enhancement after the injection of contrast (Figure 1d).

report.source_text: Histopathological examination of the thoracic lesion revealed small round cells with moderate pleomorphism, nuclear atypia, and some true rosette formations in a pauci-vascular background (Figure 3a). Immunohistochemical staining of the tumor showed diffuse, strong immunoreactivity for cluster of differentiation (CD)99, and a high proliferative index (Ki-67: 85%–90%), with negative staining for leukocyte common antigen (LCA) (Figure 3b–d).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 46-year-old woman with a history of Ewing sarcoma, previously considered cured, presented with progressive paraparesis and paresthesia. MRI of the spine revealed a huge intramedullary thoracic lesion (T5-T8) and a round intradural extramedullary mass at L1-L2. Histopathological examination of the thoracic lesion confirmed Ewing sarcoma, showing small round cells with moderate pleomorphism, nuclear atypia, rosette formations, diffuse strong CD99 immunoreactivity, high Ki-67, and negative LCA. Postoperative imaging showed appropriate decompression of the thoracic spine and complete resolution of the L1-L2 lumbosacral lesion. At 10-month follow-up, the patient's neurological status had worsened significantly, and she was alive with disease.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with progressive paraparesis and paresthesia, with a history of Ewing sarcoma.
MRI revealed a huge intramedullary thoracic lesion (T5-T8) and a round intradural extramedullary mass at L1-L2.
Histopathological examination of the thoracic lesion showed small round cells, CD99 positivity, high Ki-67, and negative LCA, consistent with Ewing sarcoma.
Postoperative imaging showed appropriate decompression of the thoracic spine and complete resolution of the L1-L2 lumbosacral lesion.
At 10-month follow-up, neurological status worsened with severe motor deficits and urofecal retention; patient was alive with disease.
